title: DIMSTYLE DIMJOGANG typed DXF projection and downgrade guard
scope: Parse and emit typed DIMJOGANG group 50 for the bounded R2007+ profile
Retain zero as the unset/default state; validate nonzero angles against Autodesk's 5-to-90 setting range
Reject nondefault typed or dynamic values when targeting pre-R2007 DXF, before writing record bytes

formatReferences.title: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1, §20.4.68
formatReferences.finding: The R2007+ DIMSTYLE DWG field inventory assigns DIMJOGANG a BD body field and group-code identity 50; this confirms DWG layout, not the DXF projection.

formatReferences.title: Autodesk DIMJOGANG system variable
formatReferences.finding: DIMJOGANG controls the transverse segment of a jogged radius dimension; Autodesk documents valid settings from 5 through 90.

formatReferences.title: LibreDWG manual, DIMSTYLE fields
formatReferences.finding: The independent open-source implementation documents DIMJOGANG as DXF group 50.

formatReferences.title: ezdxf DIMSTYLE table documentation
formatReferences.finding: The R2007+ group-50 mapping is explicitly classified as unofficial and describes the value as the jog angle.

formatReferences.title: Autodesk DIMSTYLE DXF reference
formatReferences.finding: The published DIMSTYLE record schema does not list group 50; the new projection is peer-documented compatibility, not an Autodesk-documented DXF guarantee.

localSource.finding: DIMSTYLE parsing and typed synchronization retain group 50. AC1021+ output emits the typed double unless a dynamic override exists; zero remains omitted. Nonzero values outside 5..90 and nonfinite values fail. Typed and dynamic nonzero values are atomically refused for older targets. Dynamic checks run before the version-specific skip, closing the discovered fail-open.

focusedTest.result: PASS (1/1; ASCII/Binary typed output/readback, typed/dynamic downgrade refusal/retry, and atomic refusal/retry for out-of-range and nonfinite angles)

remaining: Autodesk's published DIMSTYLE DXF schema omits group 50; producer-authored and native-consumer validation remain necessary before any broader claim.
